findings.quote: Pain that lasts more than a day or two, or comes with fever or swelling, needs a prompt exam.
findings.why: Fever or swelling with a toothache can signal a spreading infection that needs same-day urgent care, and the post's own intro sends swelling that spreads to the face or neck to an emergency room, so 'prompt exam' understates the urgency.
findings.fix: Replace with: Fever or swelling with a toothache needs same-day dental care, and if swelling spreads to your face or neck, or you have trouble breathing or swallowing, go to an emergency room or call 911.

findings.quote: The ADA's [MouthHealthy page on dental emergencies](https://www.mouthhealthy.org/all-topics-a-z/dental-emergencies) lists common cases and what to do.
findings.why: The link plausibly supports the claim, but I could not confirm that this exact URL path resolves, so it should be checked before publication.
findings.fix: Open the link to confirm it resolves to the ADA MouthHealthy dental emergencies page, and update the path if it does not.

findings.quote: Our emergency dental care is led by Dr. Elena Marsh.
findings.why: The ficha lists emergency care as one of Dr. Marsh's focus areas but does not say she leads the service, so 'led by' is stronger than the source supports.
findings.fix: Reword to: Dr. Elena Marsh, who focuses on emergency care, is one of our dentists for these visits.

findings.quote: Dental emergencies rarely happen at a convenient time.
findings.why: This generic opener reads like stock AI copy and adds no specific information for the reader.
findings.fix: Open with a concrete scenario, such as a tooth that cracked while eating, and state the first step to take.
